paragraphs.title: Abijah's Rise and the Conflict with Jeroboam

easy.explanation: The first verse says that Abijah began to reign over Judah.
Abijah reigned three years in Jerusalem.
easy.q: How many years did Abijah reign in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: The passage says there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

medium.explanation: Abijah's army consisted of four hundred thousand chosen men.
medium.q: How many chosen men did Abijah set in battle array?

medium.explanation: Jeroboam set eight hundred thousand chosen men against Abijah's four hundred thousand.
medium.q: What numerical advantage did Jeroboam's army have?

answers: Prepared and arranged the army for battle
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Abijah arranged and prepared his army for battle.
medium.q: What does “set the battle in array” mean in this passage?

answers: The conflict involved two large armies
challenge.explanation: The numbers show that both sides prepared for a major battle, although Jeroboam had the larger army.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the two army figures given at the beginning of the chapter?

answers: Abijah became king, and then the armies prepared for war
Asa became king, and then Abijah was born
Jeroboam died, and then Abijah began to reign
challenge.explanation: The passage first describes Abijah's reign and then the military preparations against Jeroboam.
challenge.q: What sequence is described in the opening verses?

answers: A military conflict between Judah and Jeroboam
The assignment of duties in the Temple
The building of a new city
challenge.explanation: The verses focus on the war and the preparation of both armies.
challenge.q: What is the main focus of these verses?

paragraphs.title: Abijah's Speech About Davidic Kingship and the Worship of God

easy.explanation: Abijah said, “Hear me, thou Jeroboam, and all Israel.”
Abijah said that the LORD gave the kingdom to David and his sons by a covenant of salt.
easy.q: To whom did Abijah say that the kingdom over Israel was given?

answers: He established peace in the land
easy.explanation: Jeroboam is described as having risen up and rebelled against his lord.
easy.q: What did Jeroboam do, according to Abijah's speech?

answers: He made golden calves and appointed unauthorized priests
He reduced the number of soldiers
medium.explanation: Abijah criticized Jeroboam for making golden calves and making priests after the manner of other nations.
medium.q: What was one of Abijah's chief criticisms of Jeroboam?

answers: Judah kept the priests, Levites, sacrifices, incense, and Temple service
Judah offered no sacrifices at all
medium.explanation: Abijah described the sons of Aaron and the Levites serving the LORD and the regular Temple worship.
medium.q: Why did Abijah present Judah's worship as faithful to the LORD?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that the shewbread was arranged on the pure table.
medium.q: What does “set they in order” mean in the phrase about the shewbread?

answers: He presented the war as a conflict against the kingdom God had given to David's sons
He claimed there was no connection between the kingdoms
He announced that David's kingdom had ended
challenge.explanation: Abijah based his claim on God's covenant with David and portrayed Judah as the kingdom of David's sons.
challenge.q: What connection did Abijah make between Davidic kingship and the present war?

answers: Judah kept the worship of the LORD, while Israel had forsaken Him and served golden calves
Judah served golden calves, while Israel kept the Temple worship
Both kingdoms had forsaken the LORD
challenge.explanation: Abijah presented Judah as faithful to the LORD and Israel as having abandoned Him.
challenge.q: What contrast did Abijah make between Judah and Israel?

answers: It connected the priests' worship with Judah's preparation for the conflict
It showed that the battle had already ended
It indicated that the priests had left Judah
challenge.explanation: The priests and their trumpets were part of Judah's religious service and its warning before battle.
challenge.q: What significance did Abijah's mention of the sounding trumpets have?

answers: He brought an ambush around behind them
easy.explanation: Jeroboam caused an ambushment to come behind Judah.
easy.q: What did Jeroboam do to Judah militarily?

easy.explanation: When Judah saw the battle before and behind, they cried unto the LORD.
easy.q: To whom did the men of Judah cry?

answers: God smote Jeroboam and all Israel
medium.explanation: After Judah shouted, God smote Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
medium.q: What happened after the men of Judah gave a shout?

answers: Because they relied upon the LORD God of their fathers
Because Judah had the larger army
medium.explanation: The passage says that Judah prevailed because they relied upon the LORD.
medium.q: Why did Judah prevail, according to the passage?

answers: A force hidden in order to attack by surprise
medium.explanation: The ambushment was Jeroboam's hidden force positioned behind Judah.
medium.q: What is an “ambushment” in this passage?

answers: Judah went from being surrounded to attacking and winning
Judah went from victory to fleeing
challenge.explanation: Although Judah was surrounded at first, the people cried to the LORD and prevailed.
challenge.q: What change took place in Judah's situation during the battle?

answers: The surprise attack did not keep Judah from calling upon the LORD and acting
Judah did not notice the ambush
The ambush caused Judah to stop fighting
challenge.explanation: Despite being surrounded, Judah cried to the LORD and the priests sounded the trumpets.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between the ambush and Judah's response emphasize?

answers: Israel fled, and five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell
The two sides made a peace covenant
challenge.explanation: The children of Israel fled, and five hundred thousand chosen men were slain.
challenge.q: What was the result of the battle?

paragraphs.title: The Pursuit of Jeroboam and the Capture of Cities

easy.q: Whom did Abijah pursue after the victory?

easy.explanation: Abijah took cities and the towns connected with them.

answers: The LORD struck him, and he died
He captured the cities of Judah
easy.explanation: The passage says that the LORD struck Jeroboam, and he died.

medium.explanation: Bethel and the towns thereof are listed among the places Abijah took.
medium.q: Which city is named among those Abijah took?

answers: Jeroboam could not regain his power against Abijah
medium.explanation: The statement describes Jeroboam's inability to recover his strength or resist Abijah.
medium.q: What does “Neither did Jeroboam recover strength again” mean?

answers: Abijah pursued Jeroboam and took cities from him
The cities were taken before the war began
Jeroboam took the cities while Abijah retreated
medium.explanation: After the victory, Abijah pursued Jeroboam and captured cities and their towns.
medium.q: What was the relationship between Abijah's pursuit and the capture of the cities?

answers: Pursuit, capture of cities, loss of Jeroboam's strength, and his death
Jeroboam's death, then the beginning of the war, and finally the capture of cities
Capture of cities, Abijah's retreat, and Jeroboam's strengthening
challenge.explanation: This is the order of events given in the passage.
challenge.q: What sequence of results is described in these verses?

answers: The conquest included settlements surrounding the cities
The cities were unrelated to the war
challenge.explanation: The wording indicates that surrounding towns were taken along with the cities.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the mention of cities and “the towns thereof”?

challenge.explanation: The passage states that the LORD struck Jeroboam and that he died.
challenge.q: Who is presented as the ultimate cause of Jeroboam's downfall?

paragraphs.title: The End of Abijah's Reign and Asa's Succession

easy.explanation: The passage says that Abijah married fourteen wives.
easy.q: How many wives did Abijah marry?

easy.explanation: The chapter says that the land had rest for ten years.
easy.q: How long did the land have rest in the days of Asa?

medium.explanation: Abijah begat twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
medium.q: How many sons and daughters did Abijah have?

answers: In the story of the prophet Iddo
In the book of the kings of Israel
medium.explanation: The verse says they were written in the story of the prophet Iddo.
medium.q: Where were the rest of Abijah's acts and ways written?

medium.explanation: This is a biblical expression describing Abijah's death and burial.
medium.q: What does “Abijah ... slept with his fathers” mean?

answers: Abijah died, Asa succeeded him, and the land had rest
Asa died, Abijah succeeded him, and the land went to war
Jeroboam succeeded Abijah, and the land had rest
challenge.explanation: The closing passage describes Abijah's death, Asa's succession, and a period of rest.
challenge.q: What was the succession described at the end of the chapter?

answers: The chapter focuses on war but ends with a period of rest
The chapter focuses on peace but ends with war
The chapter begins with Asa's reign and ends with Abijah's reign
challenge.explanation: The chapter describes battle and victory, then mentions ten years of peace.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the main part of the chapter and its ending?

answers: Another source contained further details about Abijah
No details about Abijah were recorded
The source described only Asa's reign
challenge.explanation: The verse points readers to another record containing the rest of Abijah's acts, ways, and sayings.
challenge.q: What may be inferred from the reference to “the story of the prophet Iddo”?
